habitat: Bare rocky outcrops and escarpments with wooded slopes, on granite, sandstone, quartzite, schist or dolomite. It sometimes roosts on buildings. SABAP1 treats it as resident through most of its range.
summary: A large nightjar of rocks. At a distance it looks dark grey or nearly black. Closer, the upperparts are freckled white, cinnamon and pale buff, and the underparts are dark brown with whitish and cinnamon barring. In flight the male has small white spots on the four outer primaries and white tips on the two outer tail feathers. The female has three or four smaller white spots on the outer primaries and no white on the outer tail. The white spots are generally hidden when the wings are folded.

similar.note: Fiery-necked Nightjar roosts on leaf litter in woodland. Freckled Nightjar roosts on bare rock and looks nearly black at a distance.

viewNotes.note: Dark and freckled, pressed to rock. The white wing spots are hidden.
No bold face pattern. It lacks prominent markings.
Male: small white spots on the four outer primaries. Female: three or four smaller spots.
Dark brown underparts with pale barring. The underwing was not named separately.

calls.description: No call was described in the Wikipedia or SABAP1 texts consulted. The file is grade A, catalogued as song, from Pretoria. The filename is donkernaguil, the Afrikaans name.

research.note: Newman has no page. Wikipedia and SABAP1 give no total length, so size is omitted. Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. SABAP1 says it is probably resident through most of its range, with local dry-season movement in some other regions. Those movements were not applied as a Kruger absence. The call text is a gap. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
